kaigo-language-session-4-notes.heading: Grooming roles, timing and independence: reading points
paragraphs: 入れ歯 and 義歯 both refer to artificial teeth replacing missing ones. The name alone does not establish who removed them, where they were stored or whether care is complete. 歯磨き means brushing teeth and is one part of oral care. Finished toothbrushing does not establish that all necessary oral care is complete.

身だしなみ means arranging appearance according to cleanliness, preferences and activities. 身支度 means preparing for upcoming activities, for example by dressing. They overlap in some situations but are not uniformly interchangeable.

パンツ may mean trousers or underwear depending on context. 下着 means clothing worn underneath other clothes. 着替え can refer either to changing clothes or to clothes to change into. 更衣 means changing clothes. If the requested item is unclear, ask which garment is meant.

診る is used for medical examination by a doctor, dentist or similar professional. Distinguish it from 見る, simply looking or observing. 夜中 means the middle of the night. Even if the account is heard this morning, do not change the event time from the middle of the night to morning in the record.

‘Dressing planned’ does not mean dressing is complete. A plan concerns something intended for the future. When adding who performed it or when, communicate based on stated facts or actual checks. Practice explaining: ‘The plan is known, but implementation remains unconfirmed.’

For giving and receiving items, distinguish the giver, recipient and deliverer. In a learning example, ‘My friend gave me a postcard’ means the friend gave it and the person received it. The same event can be expressed as ‘I received a postcard from my friend.’ Neither sentence identifies who delivered it to the facility.

‘Like best’ means the strongest preference within a comparison. Saying ‘I like looking at flowers best’ in a learning example does not mean disliking other activities. An activity chosen today is not necessarily the usual favorite either. Report the degree of preference separately from the current choice.

kaigo-reading-new-225.heading: Separate schedule creation, checking and distribution
paragraphs:
Worker A: Who made this dressing schedule?
Worker B: I made it yesterday. The person responsible checked it this morning.
Worker A: Who gave it to the residents?
Worker B: The reception worker. I did not take it to them.
Worker A: So different people created, checked and distributed it?
Worker B: Yes. Creation and checking were on different days too.

Worker B created it yesterday, the person responsible checked this morning, and the reception worker handed it to residents. B explicitly says they did not deliver it. Match creator, checker and distributor separately and distinguish yesterday from this morning. The dialogue does not say whether residents have changed clothes.

kaigo-reading-new-226.heading: The missing-item stage and checks still to come
paragraphs:
Resident: I haven’t been able to find my denture case since the middle of the night.
Worker: So you didn’t first notice this morning?
Resident: That’s right. I searched at night and again in the morning.
Worker: I will check with the responsible worker and let you know if it is found.
Resident: It still hasn’t been found?
Worker: Correct. We cannot yet say we know where it is stored.

The case has been missing since the middle of the night, and the person searched at night and in the morning. They did not first notice this morning. The worker will check with the responsible colleague and notify them if it is found. Neither discovery nor storage location is confirmed; do not report either as established.

kaigo-reading-new-227.heading: Clothes to send and a jacket to keep
paragraphs:
Resident: I want to separate clothes for laundry.
Worker: Shall we put them in the box on the right?
Resident: No. The right side is returned clothing. Clothes going out go on the left.
Worker: I have checked the labels. I will put them on the left.
Resident: Please keep the jacket here. I will use it this afternoon.
Worker: I will separate the other clothes without sending the jacket.

Here, the right box holds returned clothes; the left is for outgoing laundry. The worker has checked labels but does not state that sorting is complete. The person wants to keep the jacket for afternoon use. The reply preserves both left/right instructions and the item not to send.

kaigo-reading-new-228.heading: Independent adjustments and requested observation
paragraphs:
Worker: I adjusted the mirror’s angle a little while ago.
Resident: Thank you. I can check my appearance while seeing my face.
Worker: Shall I help straighten your collar too?
Resident: I can do the collar myself. Just tell me how the back looks.
Worker: Understood. I will look at the back and tell you.
Resident: I don’t need everything done for me.

The worker adjusted the mirror, and that task is complete. The person can straighten their collar, but completion is not stated. The request is to look at the back and describe it. Neither helping with everything nor providing no support matches their wishes.

kaigo-language-session-4-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: grooming roles, timing and independence
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
衣類（いるい） — Clothing: garments worn on the body.
入れ歯（いれば） — Dentures: an everyday word for artificial teeth replacing missing teeth.
うがい（うがい） — Rinsing the mouth or gargling. Check the specific method and whether it is possible according to condition and support methods.
上着（うわぎ） — Upper garment: clothing worn on the upper body; here, an outer garment such as a jacket.
着替え（きがえ） — Changing clothes; also the clothes prepared for changing.
義歯（ぎし） — Dentures: artificial teeth replacing missing teeth, also called ireba.
起床（きしょう） — Getting up from bed.
くし（くし） — Comb: a tool for combing and arranging hair.
更衣（こうい） — Changing clothes.
口腔ケア（こうくうけあ） — Oral care: care supporting cleanliness and health of the mouth, including teeth and gums.
下着（したぎ） — Underwear: clothing worn beneath outer garments.
スカート（すかーと） — Skirt: a garment covering below the waist without separate leg sections.
爪きり（つめきり） — Nail clippers: a tool for cutting nails. In this exercise, learn the name without performing untrained actions.
とかす（とかす） — Comb: here, arrange hair using a comb.
ドライヤー（どらいやー） — Hair dryer: a device that blows air to dry hair. Take care with heat.
ねまき（ねまき） — Clothing worn for sleeping.
歯医者（はいしゃ） — A common word for dentist; sometimes also a dental clinic.
歯ブラシ（はぶらし） — Toothbrush: a brush for cleaning teeth.
歯磨き（はみがき） — Toothbrushing: cleaning teeth with a toothbrush or similar item.
パンツ（ぱんつ） — Trousers or underwear, depending on context. Check if the intended meaning is unclear.
ひげ剃り（ひげそり） — Shaving facial hair; sometimes also the shaving tool.
みだしなみ（みだしなみ） — Grooming: arranging appearance for cleanliness, personal preferences and activities.
ゆすぐ（ゆすぐ） — When referring to the mouth, rinsing with water or another suitable liquid. Check the specific method against the person’s condition.
左側（ひだりがわ） — The left side from a reference person or object. Also check whose viewpoint is used.
右側（みぎがわ） — The right side from a reference person or object. Also check whose viewpoint is used.
診る（みる） — To medically examine, as a doctor or dentist does. Distinguish this from simply looking.
夜中（よなか） — The middle of the night. Read it as the event time, separately from when the account was heard.
診察（しんさつ） — A doctor or dentist checks health by listening to the person and examining their body or condition. Distinguish this role from a care worker’s observation.

kaigo-language-session-5-notes.heading: Hygiene-support scope and sign changes: reading points
paragraphs: Even after dressing, a separate task such as attaching a name badge may remain. Ask what is difficult and how much the person wants to do themselves, and confirm consent for the needed part. Permission for partial help does not authorize taking over everything.

When checking temperature, specify whether it is water, room air or an object’s surface. ぬるい expresses a feeling that something is not very hot or not as warm as expected. The word alone cannot determine a safe water temperature or device setting. Check the difficulty and consult the person responsible about necessary adjustments.

清拭 means wiping the body clean, 洗髪 washing hair and 洗面 washing the face. 洗面器 is a container for water, unlike a fixed washbasin. 浴室 is the bathing room, 浴槽 the tub holding bathing water, and 脱衣室 the room for undressing and dressing. Distinguish what is done from where it happens.

消毒 is a process that reduces infection risk by reducing pathogens or similar means; 消毒液 is the chemical liquid used. Distinguish the action from the material. 清潔保持 means maintaining cleanliness; a record of that alone does not prove disinfection occurred. This vocabulary practice does not instruct selection of disinfectant types or concentrations.

In ‘checked the hair-washing schedule,’ the completed action is checking the schedule. Hair washing itself is not stated as complete. Read words with several meanings, such as かける or かく, together with their objects. Pouring water, applying brakes and sweating are different actions.

kaigo-reading-new-229.heading: Help only with the name badge
paragraphs:
Resident: I have changed clothes. I would also like my name badge on.
Worker: Can you use the fastener?
Resident: I opened it and tried, but I cannot fasten it properly.
Worker: May I help just with attaching the badge?
Resident: Yes. I have already chosen my clothes, so please don’t change them.
Worker: Keep the clothes as they are, and just the badge.

Dressing is complete and the person chose the clothes. They opened and tried the fastener but could not attach the badge properly. Consent is for help attaching it without changing the current clothes. Even at the dialogue’s end, badge attachment is not reported as complete.

kaigo-reading-new-231.heading: Larger lettering and an unchecked arrow
paragraphs:
Worker A: The bathroom-entrance sign is easier to read than yesterday.
Worker B: The lettering is larger, but I haven’t checked the directional arrow yet.
Worker A: So we cannot yet say the entire sign is clearer.
Worker B: Yes. I would like to ask residents for their views too.
Worker A: Let’s record a before-and-after comparison.
Worker B: I will record text size separately from unchecked details.

Worker A compares the sign with yesterday. B confirmed larger lettering, while the arrow remains unchecked. Residents’ views also remain to be asked. One change does not establish that all guidance is clear. Separate changed and unconfirmed details in the record.

kaigo-reading-new-232.heading: When a change starts and today’s wishes
paragraphs:
Resident: Yesterday’s notice said the face-washing location will change.
Worker: The change starts next week. Today we use the usual place.
Resident: So not the new location today?
Worker: Correct. Let’s check today’s directions first.
Resident: I only want to know the location now. I would like to wash my face this afternoon.
Worker: Check the location now; face washing this afternoon.

The change announced yesterday begins next week; today’s face-washing location remains unchanged. The person only wants location information now, not immediate face washing. Location is checked now; washing is preferred in the afternoon. Distinguish the notice-reading date, change start date and preferred activity time.

kaigo-language-session-5-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: hygiene-support scope and sign changes
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
温度（おんど） — Temperature: degree of hotness or coldness. Identify whether it is room, water or another temperature.
かける（かける） — A verb whose meaning depends on its object. お湯をかける means pouring water; ブレーキをかける means applying brakes.
かく（かく） — In 汗をかく, to sweat. Distinguish it from writing or scratching skin through context.
シャンプー（しゃんぷー） — Shampoo: a product for washing hair and scalp.
消毒（しょうどく） — Processing that reduces infection risk, for example by reducing pathogens. This practice does not involve choosing products or concentrations.
消毒液（しょうどくえき） — Chemical liquid used for disinfection. Knowing the name differs from judging suitable products and use.
清潔保持（せいけつほじ） — Maintaining hygiene: keeping necessary cleanliness through methods suited to the person.
清拭（せいしき） — Wiping the body clean with towels or similar items, either the whole body or part of it.
洗髪（せんぱつ） — Hair washing: washing the hair and scalp, separate from completed drying or styling.
洗面（せんめん） — Face washing.
洗面器（せんめんき） — A container for water used to wash the face or body. Distinguish it from a fixed washbasin.
脱衣室（だついしつ） — Changing room: a room for undressing or dressing before or after bathing and similar activities.
入浴（にゅうよく） — Bathing: cleaning the body by methods such as entering bathwater. Follow the plan for the specific method.
ぬるい（ぬるい） — Feeling that something is not very hot or not as warm as expected. It is not a numerical safe temperature.
拭く（ふく） — Wipe: remove moisture or dirt with cloth, a towel or a similar item.
浴室（よくしつ） — Bathroom: a room for washing the body or using a bathtub.
浴槽（よくそう） — Bathtub: equipment holding water for immersing the body, not the whole bathroom.
リンス（りんす） — A product used during hair washing to condition the hair.
確認（かくにん） — Checking or confirming: asking about or looking into something unclear to establish what is correct.

kaigo-language-session-6-notes.heading: Read hygiene explanations by degree, direction and conditions
paragraphs: 〜にくい means an action is difficult, not necessarily impossible. 〜やすい means it is easy. Even a ‘slip-resistant floor’ does not guarantee that slipping can never occur. Preserve degree rather than changing it to categorical impossibility or guaranteed success.

When reading ‘from…to…’ or ‘toward…,’ identify the starting point and destination. One-way guidance alone does not determine the return route or direction. Match symbols such as circles and stars to the explanation on that specific diagram.

Ask separately what should change and what can stay as it is. ‘I will check whether it can be changed’ means checking possibility is still ahead, not that settings have been changed. A wish following ‘if that is not possible’ applies under that condition. Do not assume the outcome before checking.

‘Difficult to hear’ alone does not establish inability to hear any sound. Check specific difficulties such as speech speed, surrounding noise and location, and ask the preferred method. In today’s scene, distinguish a wish to change volume from a wish to change speed.

kaigo-reading-new-233.heading: Specify the part that is difficult to read
paragraphs:
Resident: I can see the shelf numbers in the changing room, but they are a little hard to read.
Worker: So you are not unable to see them at all?
Resident: Correct. The small lettering below the numbers is hard to make out.
Worker: I will check numbers and small lettering separately.
Resident: Please don’t report that I cannot read any of it.
Worker: I will report that some parts are difficult to read.

The person can see the shelf numbers and describes some reading difficulty, especially with small text below them. They ask not to be described as unable to read anything. In reporting, distinguish numbers from small text and visibility from reading difficulty, preserving scope and degree.

kaigo-reading-new-234.heading: Starting point and destination in one diagram
paragraphs:
Worker A: The arrow in this diagram goes from the changing room toward reception.
Worker B: Isn’t it guidance from reception to the changing room?
Worker A: No. The circle marks the starting point and the star the destination.
Worker B: On this paper, the circle is the changing room.
Worker A: Yes. The return route has a separate diagram.
Worker B: We shouldn’t assume both diagrams point the same way.

In this learning scene’s diagram, the circle is the changing-room starting point and the star is reception, the destination. The arrow goes toward reception. The return route is on another diagram, so this paper alone cannot explain returning from reception to the changing room. Circle and star meanings belong to this example, not a universal facility-sign convention.

kaigo-reading-new-235.heading: Change speed, not volume
paragraphs:
Resident: I want to hear the bathing guidance, but the recorded voice is fast.
Worker: Shall I increase the volume?
Resident: The volume is fine. I only want the speed changed.
Worker: I will check whether playback can be slowed.
Resident: If it cannot, please explain in short sections.
Worker: First I will check the settings and tell you the result.

The person says volume is fine and wants only speed changed. The worker has yet to check whether playback can be slowed. If not, the person wants an explanation in short sections. Neither settings changes nor explanation is established as complete.

kaigo-reading-new-236.heading: Closed here now; viewing later in the corridor
paragraphs:
Resident: Please close the curtain while I hear the explanation of the bed bath.
Worker: You also said you wanted to see the notice.
Resident: Yes, but I will look at it in the corridor.
Worker: So we should not open the curtain here for the explanation?
Resident: Keep it closed here. I want to see the notice later.
Worker: I will separate the current explanation from seeing the notice later.

The person wants the curtain closed during the bed-bath explanation here and now. The notice will be viewed later in the corridor, so the wishes concern different places and times. Wanting to see the notice is not consent to opening the curtain now. Also check the wish to hear an explanation separately from consent to the bed bath itself.

kaigo-language-session-6-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: degree, direction and conditions
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
〜にくい（〜にくい） — Expresses difficulty performing an action, not categorical inability.
〜やすい（〜やすい） — Expresses ease of performing an action, not guaranteed success.
〜から〜へ（〜から〜へ） — Connects a starting place with a destination. It does not specify the return route.
〜できるか確認する（〜できるかかくにんする） — Check whether something is possible. Possibility or completed action is not yet established.
〜できなければ（〜できなければ） — If it is not possible. Read the following wish or method together with this condition.

kaigo-language-session-7-notes.heading: Household information sources and participation scope: reading points
paragraphs: Equipment quantities, personal wishes and staff responsibilities are separate checks. A responsible worker confirming quantities does not mean the person expressed a preference. Clarify who supplied which information; do not substitute schedules or inventory for personal choice.

乾かす means making something dry. 乾く means becoming dry; 干す means spreading or hanging something out for drying or similar purposes. ‘Hung out’ does not necessarily mean already dry. ‘Dry’ alone does not identify who hung it out. Do not add an unstated next task.

掃く and 吐く are both read はく but mean different things. Check characters and context to distinguish sweeping rubbish with a broom from vomiting as a bodily event. Do not misread a household record as a symptom record.

おしぼり is a damp cloth or similar item mainly for wiping hands; a mop is a cleaning tool for floors and similar surfaces. Household work includes cleaning, laundry and cooking. Cooking means preparing meals. Participation may consist of describing household experience; the speaker does not necessarily take responsibility for every task.

‘The laundry was hung out, but it is not dry yet’ means hanging is complete but dryness has not been reached. Rewriting it as ‘the dry items were put away’ removes the negative and adds unstated storage. Explain completed actions separately from states not yet reached.

kaigo-reading-new-237.heading: Supply checks differ from personal-wish checks
paragraphs:
Worker A: I checked the bathroom supplies with the person responsible.
Worker B: So you know the resident’s wishes too?
Worker A: No, only the quantity of supplies. I haven’t asked their wishes yet.
Worker B: I will ask the person directly.
Worker A: Yes. Please don’t decide from the schedule alone.
Worker B: Equipment checks and personal choices are separate.

Worker A checked only supply quantities with the person responsible. Personal wishes have not been asked; B will ask next. A responsible person’s check or an existing schedule does not prove a personal choice. Equipment counts also do not establish completed health checks or assistance.

kaigo-reading-new-239.heading: Separate counting participation from carrying
paragraphs:
Worker: We plan to make an equipment list during the household activity.
Resident: I can help count. I won’t carry things.
Worker: Will you take them to the shelf after counting?
Resident: No, only counting. Please have someone else carry them.
Worker: Understood. I will write the numbers on the list.
Resident: Then please call me when you start.

The person offers counting only and declines carrying. The worker will write numbers on the list. Someone else is needed to carry, but that person is not identified yet. The request to be called at the start does not state that work has begun.

kaigo-reading-new-240.heading: Participate by sharing memories
paragraphs:
Resident: In next month’s cooking activity, I would like to introduce menus from the past.
Worker: Are you planning to cook them yourself?
Resident: Not cook; I will tell everyone my memories.
Worker: You will need time to talk with the cooking staff too.
Resident: Yes. What to make has not been decided.
Worker: I will convey your wish to introduce them and that the menu is undecided.

The person wants to share memories of old menus next month, not cook independently. Time to talk with cooking staff is needed, but the menu remains undecided. It is not stated that cooking staff have already accepted particular dishes. The worker separately conveys the participation wish and undecided menu.

kaigo-language-session-7-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: household information and participation
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
おしぼり（おしぼり） — A damp cloth or similar item mainly for wiping hands. Distinguish it from floor-cleaning tools.
カーテン（かーてん） — Curtain: fabric covering windows or spaces to adjust light or screen views.
家事（かじ） — Housework: tasks maintaining daily life, such as cooking, cleaning and laundry.
片付ける（かたづける） — Put away: organize items into agreed places, not discard them without permission.
乾かす（かわかす） — To reduce moisture and make something dry. Distinguish it from the change of state described by 乾く.
乾く（かわく） — For moisture to decrease and something to become dry. It does not describe who did what.
換気（かんき） — Ventilation: replace indoor air with outside air.
シーツ（しーつ） — Sheet: fabric covering bedding.
洗濯物（せんたくもの） — Laundry: items awaiting washing or already washed. Check the processing stage too.
掃除機（そうじき） — Vacuum cleaner: a machine removing dust and debris by suction.
たたむ（たたむ） — Fold: arrange fabric in overlapping layers, distinct from washing or hanging it.
調理（ちょうり） — Cooking: handling ingredients and preparing edible dishes.
掃く（はく） — To gather or remove rubbish and dust with a broom or similar tool. It differs from 吐く, vomiting.
布団（ふとん） — Bedding laid beneath or placed over someone for sleep. Check which is meant from context.
ほうき（ほうき） — A broom for sweeping rubbish and dust from floors or similar surfaces.
干す（ほす） — To spread or hang something for drying or similar purposes. It need not be dry immediately afterward.
枕（まくら） — A pillow supporting the head during sleep or similar situations.
毛布（もうふ） — A blanket: bedding used over the body or similarly for warmth.
モップ（もっぷ） — A mop: a handled cleaning tool with cloth or similar material at its end for wiping floors and other surfaces.

kaigo-language-session-8-notes.heading: Household conditions, experience and confirmed results: reading points
paragraphs: A scheduled time is decided beforehand; actual completion means the activity has really ended. If the next task depends on another activity ending, reaching the scheduled time alone does not meet the condition. Identify what must be checked with whom before proceeding.

‘Could you tell me?’ can request an explanation of a method or a description of experience. It does not necessarily delegate the whole task. If the person is uncertain, clarify whether you want to hear their account or request actual work.

When completed areas are marked, what is established is the marked part. Do not expand this to completion of everything. If unmarked areas are unchecked, they also cannot be declared unfinished. Thank the person while accurately recording what is known.

In record practice, separate confirmed from unconfirmed: ‘Marked areas are complete. Unmarked areas have not yet been checked.’ Do not replace unconfirmed with impossible, refused or complete. Also consider what needs checking to make the next judgment.

kaigo-reading-new-241.heading: Check actual activity completion, not scheduled noon
paragraphs:
Worker A: Someone said the vacuum-cleaner noise bothers them.
Worker B: Shall we use it at noon?
Worker A: Time alone does not decide it. First confirm that the activity next door has ended.
Worker B: It is scheduled until noon, but it may run over.
Worker A: Yes. Please check completion with the person responsible.
Worker B: I will distinguish scheduled time from actual completion.

Here, vacuum use depends on the activity next door actually ending. Even a noon finish on the schedule may be delayed. Read the responsibility to check completion with the person responsible before using it. This is a condition agreed in this scene, not a rule prohibiting vacuum use until noon at every facility.

kaigo-reading-new-242.heading: A request to learn from experience
paragraphs:
Resident: I have a way of arranging clothes so they are easy to find.
Worker: Could you tell me about it?
Resident: Am I supposed to put everything away?
Worker: No. I want to hear your idea, not delegate the work to you.
Resident: In that case, I will describe arranging them in order of use.
Worker: After organizing what you tell me, I will discuss the actual arrangement with you.

The worker wants to hear an idea for making clothes easy to find, not ask the person to do all the tidying. The person will describe arranging by use order; the worker will organize that information and then discuss placement. Neither changed placement nor consent to changing it is stated as complete.

kaigo-reading-new-243.heading: Marked and unchecked areas
paragraphs:
Resident: I marked the completed areas on the tidying schedule.
Worker: Thank you. Are the unmarked areas finished too?
Resident: I haven’t looked at those yet.
Worker: Now we can see which parts are finished.
Resident: Yes. Please don’t write that everything is complete.
Worker: I will record marked parts separately from unchecked parts.

The person marked finished parts and says unmarked ones have not been checked. The marks establish completed parts, not that everything is done or that unmarked parts are unfinished. The worker thanks them and records completed and unconfirmed information separately.

kaigo-language-session-8-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: household conditions, experience and results
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
予定時刻（よていじこく） — A time decided in advance. Distinguish it from the actual start or finish time.
終了（しゅうりょう） — The ending of an activity. Planned completion is not the fact of completion.
工夫（くふう） — Thinking of or improving a method to suit a purpose.
印（しるし） — A symbol or other mark used as an indicator. Check its meaning from that table’s explanation.
未確認（みかくにん） — Not yet checked. It does not mean refusal or impossibility.

kaigo-language-session-9-notes.heading: Separate condition, timing and unconfirmed details in handovers
paragraphs: When reading handovers, distinguish what the person can decide, what requires assistance and what has not been asked. Choosing clothes independently differs from putting them on alone. Supporting independence values both personal choice and assistance needs for each action.

Observation means carefully checking condition or changes. Reporting means communicating what is known to necessary recipients; handover passes needed information to workers continuing support. ‘Report sent’ alone does not confirm receipt or completed response.

A plan sets out what will be done; a change alters its content or similar details. A participant joins an activity; a service user uses a service. A name appearing in a plan alone does not establish consent to participate or actual attendance.

ケース can mean a container or a case/situation. 流行 can mean infectious-disease spread or widespread preferences or styles. 見守り means observing so necessary support can be provided. The term alone does not mean someone can do everything alone.

就寝 means going to bed to sleep, 出勤 going to work, and 退勤 finishing the day’s shift and leaving. 日勤 and 夜勤 describe working periods. Separate the report-writing time from the time of the recorded event.

‘Changed the medication schedule’ states a schedule change, not that medication was taken. This reading practice does not permit independently changing medication instructions. When checking words such as nurse call, emergency alarm or 119, do not activate real equipment or make emergency calls for practice.

kaigo-reading-new-247.heading: Independent choices and dressing help
paragraphs:
Resident handover
For morning dressing, the person chooses the type of jacket. Staff help them put their arms through the sleeves.
On some days, they do not change jackets for afternoon activities. Today’s afternoon dressing preference has not yet been asked.
Check independent choice separately from dressing alone.

The person chooses the jacket type and staff help with sleeves. Choosing clothes differs from independently completing all dressing movements. Some afternoons involve no jacket change, but today’s wish is unasked. Do not decide today’s choice from usual patterns.

kaigo-reading-new-248.heading: Recorded facts and unstated reasons
paragraphs:
Activity record
Last week’s visit was shorter than planned. The reason is not given in this record.
Today the person is talking with a worker in the lounge, not visiting family.
They sometimes ask to hear explanations again in large-group activities, but so far have not done so in today’s two-person conversation.
Their wish to attend this afternoon’s event will be checked next.

Last week’s visit was shorter than planned, but no reason is recorded. Today’s conversation is with a worker, not a family visit. Requests for repetition sometimes occur in large groups, but not so far in today’s two-person conversation. Do not generalize hearing without these conditions and timing. Afternoon attendance wishes also remain to be checked.

kaigo-language-session-9-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: handover condition, timing and uncertainty
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
観察（かんさつ） — Observation: carefully checking the person and surroundings.
行事（ぎょうじ） — Event: a planned gathering or activity.
禁止（きんし） — Prohibition: something specified as not allowed. Read the location and time scope too.
計画（けいかく） — Plan: agreed future actions, methods and timing toward a goal.
掲示（けいじ） — Notice: displaying information visibly, or the document displayed.
ケース（けーす） — May mean a container or a case/situation.
玄関（げんかん） — Entrance: a place for entering and leaving a building.
参加者（さんかしゃ） — Someone participating in an activity. Distinguish planned from actual participation.
事故（じこ） — Accident: an unintended event leading to injury, damage or similar harm.
施設（しせつ） — Facility: a building, equipment or organization providing support or services.
就寝（しゅうしん） — Going to bed to sleep.
出勤（しゅっきん） — Going to the workplace for work.
巡視（じゅんし） — Going around designated locations to check conditions.
使用（しよう） — Using an item, facility or equipment.
状況（じょうきょう） — The state of events or people at that time.
ショートステイ（しょーとすてい） — Short stay: staying briefly in a facility with needed support. Check service conditions with the consultation contact.
自立（じりつ） — Independence: acting with one’s own abilities and choosing and deciding how to live.
送迎車（そうげいしゃ） — A vehicle for picking up or taking service users or others to their destinations.
退勤（たいきん） — Finishing the day’s shift and leaving work.
タイヤ（たいや） — A tire: the component covering the outside of a vehicle’s wheel.
建物（たてもの） — A building: a structure people enter to live or undertake activities.
担当者（たんとうしゃ） — The person responsible for a task or support.
調理員（ちょうりいん） — A staff member responsible for preparing meals.
転倒（てんとう） — Fall: losing balance and falling during standing, walking or a similar activity.
ナースコール（なーすこーる） — Equipment through which the person or others contact staff to request help. This unit does not involve activating real equipment for practice.
日勤（にっきん） — A shift mainly during daytime. Check exact hours from the workplace schedule.
濡れる（ぬれる） — To become wet with water or another liquid.
吐く（はく） — To bring stomach contents back through the mouth, or to expel breath or material through it. Read what is expelled from context.
外す（はずす） — To remove or detach something attached.
非常口（ひじょうぐち） — An emergency exit for escaping outside during fire or another emergency.
非常ベル（ひじょうべる） — An alarm signaling fire or another emergency. Do not activate it for practice.
119番（ひゃくじゅうきゅうばん） — Japan’s emergency number when a fire engine or ambulance is needed. Do not call to test a connection or for learning.
服薬（ふくやく） — Taking medicine. Do not confuse plans or schedule changes with an actual administration record.
変更（へんこう） — Change: alter something decided. Also check what remains unchanged.
報告（ほうこく） — Report: communicate confirmed facts, actions, results or changes.
ホール（ほーる） — A large room or space for group activities. Its location varies by facility.
まつり（まつり） — A festival or celebratory event held in a community or facility.
ミーティング（みーてぃんぐ） — Staff or others gathering to share information or discuss matters.
見守り（みまもり） — Checking condition and actions so necessary support can be provided. It does not mean everything can be done alone.
面会（めんかい） — Visiting to meet the person. This communication method differs from letters or calls.
申し送り（もうしおくり） — Handoff: communicate and check conditions, responses and unfinished matters with the next worker to continue support.
夜勤（やきん） — A shift including nighttime. Check exact hours from the workplace schedule.
流行（りゅうこう） — Spread of infectious disease or similar phenomena; also widespread preferences or styles. Distinguish meanings through context.
利用者（りようしゃ） — Person receiving services: someone using care or other services.

kaigo-language-session-10-notes.heading: Record conditions, roles and privacy: reading points
paragraphs: Ability records may include conditions such as wearing glasses or being in a quiet room. Do not remove them and assume equal ability everywhere. ‘Not tried today’ proves neither inability nor ability.

Read activity records action by action: who chose, who acted and who supported which part. Family offers do not necessarily match personal wishes. Separately check staff reading letters or sharing private content with the person, respecting wishes and sharing scope.

When organizing information yourself, separate completed facts, what the person or family said and what remains unasked. Do not change ‘not yet asked’ into ‘refused’ or ‘cannot.’ Respecting words and explicitly identifying unconfirmed details are compatible.

kaigo-reading-new-249.heading: Conditions for reading and hearing
paragraphs:
Reading-activity record
Text: the person can read large print while wearing glasses. Small print has not been tried today.
Audio: in a quiet room, they listen to explanations at ordinary voice volume. They report difficulty hearing corridor announcements.
Choice: ask whether they prefer larger text or a worker reading aloud.

Large print is readable with glasses, but small print has not been tried today. The person listens to ordinary-volume explanations in a quiet room and reports difficulty with corridor announcements. Preserve conditions of text size, glasses, location and sound type. Larger text or staff reading remains a choice to ask about.

kaigo-reading-new-250.heading: Read gardening tasks by person and action
paragraphs:
Gardening participation record
Pot choice: the person chose the color.
Label: the person wrote the name; a worker wrote the date.
Clearing up: who will carry equipment is undecided.
Next time: before participation, check whether the same role is wanted.

The person chose the pot color and wrote the label’s name; the worker wrote the date. The equipment carrier remains undecided. Whether the same role is wanted next time will be checked before participation. Performing some parts does not establish that the person did everything or that next time’s role is decided.

kaigo-reading-new-251.heading: Personal wishes, a sister’s offer and unconfirmed consent
paragraphs:
Communication-preference interview
The person said they want to communicate by letter with their younger sister. Wishes about visits have not yet been asked.
The sister said by phone that she can send envelopes. They have not arrived yet.
Whether staff may read the letters also needs checking with the person.

The person wants letters with their younger sister. The sister offered by phone to send envelopes, but they have not arrived. Visit wishes and consent to staff reading letters remain unchecked. Do not substitute the sister’s offer for personal wishes or consent. Ask how private letter-related content should be handled.

kaigo-language-session-10-terms.heading: Word and expression reference: conditions, roles and privacy
paragraphs: This reference helps check unfamiliar words in conversations and records. It is not an assignment to learn every word anew today. Choose words used today and return when needed.
条件（じょうけん） — Circumstances or prerequisites for something to hold, including locations and equipment.
役割（やくわり） — A responsibility or task in the situation. Read choosing, writing and carrying separately.
希望（きぼう） — Wishes: what the person would like to do or have happen.
申し出（もうしで） — Telling someone one’s ideas or what one can do. It does not necessarily mean completed action.
未確認（みかくにん） — Not yet checked. It does not mean refusal or impossibility.
同意（どうい） — Agreeing to and accepting something after receiving an explanation or similar information. It does not automatically extend to another action.

148.title: Grooming roles, timing and independence
objectives: Distinguish who created, checked and distributed an item and when each action occurred.
Read what the person can do and which support they want in dressing and grooming.
148.context: Four conversations concern dressing, a denture case, laundry and a mirror. Check who did what and what remains unfinished.
148.artCaption: The person chooses clothing while a worker shows garments. Check choice separately from assistance with dressing movements.

149.title: Hygiene-support scope and sign changes
objectives: Read consent to part of a task separately from completing the whole task.
Distinguish change start dates from today’s wishes and confirmed from unconfirmed details.
149.context: These scenes concern name-badge help and bathroom or face-washing guidance. Connect word meanings with the specific actions the person wants.
149.artCaption: A worker faces the person and listens. Use the scene to practice confirming wishes and help scope before acting.

150.title: Read hygiene explanations by degree, direction and conditions
objectives: Describe reading difficulty without changing it into total inability.
Distinguish guidance direction, requested changes and conditional requests.
150.context: Conversations concern shelf labels, routes, recording speed and a curtain. Preserve place, timing and degree when receiving the person’s words.
150.artCaption: A worker arranges a basin and towels. This shows preparation, not bed-bath technique, water temperature or consent to implementation.

151.title: Household information sources and participation scope
objectives: Separate equipment checks, personal wishes and task allocation.
Distinguish participation through sharing experience from responsibility for actual work.
151.context: Conversations concern checking supplies and participating in household or cooking activities. Identify information sources without replacing personal wishes with other information.
151.artCaption: A worker listens beside glasses on a table. Consent to wiping does not necessarily extend to moving items.

152.title: Household conditions, experience and confirmed results
objectives: Distinguish scheduled time from actual completion.
Separate requests for advice from work requests, and completion from unconfirmed details.
152.context: These scenes concern vacuum-use conditions, tidying ideas and schedule marks. Combine gratitude for cooperation with accurate records.
152.artCaption: The person demonstrates handling a bag while the worker watches. Distinguish learning from experience from delegating all the work.

153.title: Separate condition, timing and unconfirmed details in handovers
objectives: Read personal choices separately from movement assistance needs.
Preserve observed-setting conditions and wishes not yet asked about.
153.context: Read a dressing handover and activity record. Do not supply unstated reasons or unasked attendance wishes through assumptions.
153.artCaption: Two workers discuss documents. Use the scene to organize reported information and checks the recipient needs to make.

154.title: Record conditions, roles and privacy
objectives: Read the conditions supporting understanding of text or voice.
Distinguish personal and family offers, actual actors and unconfirmed consent.
154.context: Read records about reading, gardening and letters. Identify abilities and wishes specifically without inferring personal consent from family statements.
154.artCaption: The person and worker discuss documents. Check wishes and scope for reading or sharing private content.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-225.prompt: Which explanation of who handed the schedule to residents matches the dialogue?
options: A reception worker handed it over, someone other than Worker B who created it.
B created it yesterday and therefore also handed it directly to residents.
The person who checked it this morning handed it over.
The reception worker was responsible only for this morning’s check.
rationales: B says creation was by B yesterday, checking by the responsible person this morning, and distribution by reception. This distinguishes distributor, creator and checker.
B created it but explicitly did not deliver it. Creation and distribution cannot be combined into one person’s actions.
The responsible person checked this morning. Reception distributed it.
The responsible person checked this morning; reception handed it to residents.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-225.reading:
Worker A: Who made this dressing schedule?
Worker B: I made it yesterday. The person responsible checked it this morning.
Worker A: Who gave it to the residents?
Worker B: The reception worker. I did not take it to them.
Worker A: So different people created, checked and distributed it?
Worker B: Yes. Creation and checking were on different days too.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-226.prompt: What is currently confirmed about the case?
options: The person first noticed it missing this morning and searched only this morning.
The responsible worker confirmed storage and the worker notified the person.
It was not found at night but was found in the morning.
It has been missing since the middle of the night; the worker will now check with the responsible colleague.
rationales: The person says it has been missing since the middle of the night and they searched at night and in the morning. Do not change first awareness to morning.
Checking with the responsible person and notification after discovery are future actions. Storage location is not yet known.
Searching again in the morning does not state discovery. The worker confirms it is still missing.
It remains missing since the middle of the night after night and morning searches. Checking is planned; discovery and storage confirmation remain incomplete.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-226.reading:
Resident: I haven’t been able to find my denture case since the middle of the night.
Worker: So you didn’t first notice this morning?
Resident: That’s right. I searched at night and again in the morning.
Worker: I will check with the responsible worker and let you know if it is found.
Resident: It still hasn’t been found?
Worker: Correct. We cannot yet say we know where it is stored.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-227.prompt: Which sorting method matches the dialogue and wishes?
options: Put laundry on the left, including the jacket needed this afternoon.
Keep the jacket and separate the other outgoing laundry on the left.
Keep the jacket and put outgoing laundry in the right box.
Move returned clothing to the left and send only the jacket to laundry.
rationales: The left location is correct, but the person wants to keep the jacket for this afternoon.
The labels place outgoing laundry on the left and returned clothes on the right. This also preserves the jacket condition.
Keeping the jacket is correct, but the right box holds returned clothes. Outgoing laundry goes left.
The left is for outgoing laundry, and the jacket must stay. Both action and target are wrong.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-227.reading:
Resident: I want to separate clothes for laundry.
Worker: Shall we put them in the box on the right?
Resident: No. The right side is returned clothing. Clothes going out go on the left.
Worker: I have checked the labels. I will put them on the left.
Resident: Please keep the jacket here. I will use it this afternoon.
Worker: I will separate the other clothes without sending the jacket.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-228.prompt: What is the person asking the worker to do?
options: The person will straighten their collar; the worker should look at the back and describe it.
The worker should adjust both mirror and collar next.
Only straighten the collar; looking at the back is declined.
Because the person can straighten their collar, looking at the back is unnecessary too.
rationales: The person can do the collar and requests only a description of the back. Independent and assisted parts match.
The worker already adjusted the mirror. The person can do the collar and is not requesting all grooming.
The collar is independent; describing the back is requested. This reverses the parts.
Some independence does not mean no support is wanted. The person requests a description of the back.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-228.reading:
Worker: I adjusted the mirror’s angle a little while ago.
Resident: Thank you. I can check my appearance while seeing my face.
Worker: Shall I help straighten your collar too?
Resident: I can do the collar myself. Just tell me how the back looks.
Worker: Understood. I will look at the back and tell you.
Resident: I don’t need everything done for me.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-229.prompt: What scope of support did the person consent to?
options: Have the worker choose different clothes to make attaching the badge easier.
Help only open the fastener, declining help attaching the badge.
Keep the chosen clothes and help only with attaching the badge.
Start dressing again and attach the badge at the end.
rationales: The person has chosen clothes and asks not to change them. Badge consent cannot extend to changing clothes.
They tried opening the fastener but could not secure it. They agree to help attaching the badge.
They accept help only with badge attachment and request unchanged clothes. Actual completed attachment is not yet stated.
Dressing is already complete. Consent covers the badge, not restarting dressing.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-229.reading:
Resident: I have changed clothes. I would also like my name badge on.
Worker: Can you use the fastener?
Resident: I opened it and tried, but I cannot fasten it properly.
Worker: May I help just with attaching the badge?
Resident: Yes. I have already chosen my clothes, so please don’t change them.
Worker: Keep the clothes as they are, and just the badge.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-231.prompt: Which separates confirmed and unconfirmed details of the sign?
options: Both letters and arrow were checked, so all guidance is clearer.
The letters are larger; the arrow and residents’ views remain to be checked.
Letter size is unconfirmed, but residents said it is clearer.
The clearer arrow removes any need to check letter size.
rationales: Only letter size was confirmed; the arrow remains unchecked. This expands a partial check into overall improvement.
Larger letters are known, but the arrow and residents’ views remain pending. This matches the before/after comparison with separate unconfirmed details.
B states that lettering is larger. Residents’ views will be asked next.
The arrow remains unchecked. Letter size is a stated actual change; the two are not interchangeable.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-231.reading:
Worker A: The bathroom-entrance sign is easier to read than yesterday.
Worker B: The lettering is larger, but I haven’t checked the directional arrow yet.
Worker A: So we cannot yet say the entire sign is clearer.
Worker B: Yes. I would like to ask residents for their views too.
Worker A: Let’s record a before-and-after comparison.
Worker B: I will record text size separately from unchecked details.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-232.prompt: Which combination matches today’s location and the preferred face-washing time?
options: The location changes today, and the person wants to wash immediately.
Because the location changes next week, the person decided not to wash today.
The location is unchanged, and the person consents to washing immediately.
The location is unchanged, and the person wants to wash this afternoon.
rationales: The change starts next week. The person only wants location information now and washing in the afternoon.
Next week’s change is correct, but the person wants to wash this afternoon, not cancel today.
Today’s location is correct, but only location is checked now. Washing is preferred in the afternoon.
Yesterday’s notice concerns next week; today uses the usual place. Location is wanted now, washing in the afternoon.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-232.reading:
Resident: Yesterday’s notice said the face-washing location will change.
Worker: The change starts next week. Today we use the usual place.
Resident: So not the new location today?
Worker: Correct. Let’s check today’s directions first.
Resident: I only want to know the location now. I would like to wash my face this afternoon.
Worker: Check the location now; face washing this afternoon.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-233.prompt: Which report accurately preserves the person’s description?
options: Neither shelf numbers nor text below them can be seen at all.
Because the numbers are visible, no part of the sign is difficult to read.
The numbers are visible, but some parts, such as small text, are difficult to read.
Only small text is readable; the numbers cannot be seen at all.
rationales: The person can see numbers. This turns slight reading difficulty into total inability to see.
Visible numbers do not mean no reading difficulty. The person identifies small text as difficult.
The person sees numbers with some difficulty and finds small text below them unclear. This preserves scope and degree without reporting total inability.
Numbers are visible; small text below them is especially difficult. This reverses targets and difficulty.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-233.reading:
Resident: I can see the shelf numbers in the changing room, but they are a little hard to read.
Worker: So you are not unable to see them at all?
Resident: Correct. The small lettering below the numbers is hard to make out.
Worker: I will check numbers and small lettering separately.
Resident: Please don’t report that I cannot read any of it.
Worker: I will report that some parts are difficult to read.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-234.prompt: Which explanation of the arrow matches the dialogue?
options: It guides from the changing room marked by a circle to reception marked by a star.
It guides from reception marked by a circle to the changing room marked by a star.
It guides back from star-marked reception to the circle-marked changing room.
One page shows both the reception route and the return to the changing room.
rationales: The circle marks the start and is the changing room here; the star marks the destination. Thus the arrow goes toward reception.
The circle is the changing room on this page. Starting point and destination are reversed.
The arrow goes from changing room to reception; the return has a separate diagram.
The return diagram is separate. Do not add a return route to a one-way diagram.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-234.reading:
Worker A: The arrow in this diagram goes from the changing room toward reception.
Worker B: Isn’t it guidance from reception to the changing room?
Worker A: No. The circle marks the starting point and the star the destination.
Worker B: On this paper, the circle is the changing room.
Worker A: Yes. The return route has a separate diagram.
Worker B: We shouldn’t assume both diagrams point the same way.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-235.prompt: What will the worker check first?
options: Whether the recording’s volume can be increased further.
Whether the person finished listening to a recording already slowed down.
Whether the person already understood an explanation in short sections.
Whether the recording’s playback can be slowed.
rationales: The person says volume is fine and wants only speed changed. This changes the requested property.
The worker will check possibility; neither settings changes nor post-playback checks are complete.
Short sections are requested if slowing is impossible. Settings are checked first; explanation is not complete.
The request concerns speed, not volume. The worker first checks settings, with short sections requested conditionally if slowing is impossible.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-235.reading:
Resident: I want to hear the bathing guidance, but the recorded voice is fast.
Worker: Shall I increase the volume?
Resident: The volume is fine. I only want the speed changed.
Worker: I will check whether playback can be slowed.
Resident: If it cannot, please explain in short sections.
Worker: First I will check the settings and tell you the result.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-236.prompt: Which response preserves both wishes about the curtain and notice?
options: Open the curtain here now for explanation because the person wants to see the notice.
Explain now with the curtain closed; view the notice in the corridor later.
Treat the wish to see the notice as canceled because the curtain should stay closed.
Go to the corridor immediately to view it, then return here for explanation.
rationales: The person wants the curtain closed here. Seeing the notice is not consent to opening it now.
The curtain stays closed for the current explanation; the notice is viewed later in the corridor. Separate time and place preserve both wishes.
The person explicitly wants to see it later in the corridor. Different times and places make the wishes compatible.
The person wants the notice later and explanation here now with the curtain closed. This adds a different order.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-236.reading:
Resident: Please close the curtain while I hear the explanation of the bed bath.
Worker: You also said you wanted to see the notice.
Resident: Yes, but I will look at it in the corridor.
Worker: So we should not open the curtain here for the explanation?
Resident: Keep it closed here. I want to see the notice later.
Worker: I will separate the current explanation from seeing the notice later.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-237.prompt: What has Worker A checked with the responsible person?
options: Bathroom-supply quantities; personal wishes have not yet been asked.
Bathroom-supply quantities and the use the person chose.
Personal wishes; supply quantities will be checked next.
Personal wishes in the schedule; asking the person is complete.
rationales: A checked quantities only. B will ask wishes next, so equipment checks and personal choice remain separate.
A says only quantities were checked. Wishes remain unasked.
Confirmed and unconfirmed are reversed. Quantities are checked; wishes remain to be asked.
A has not asked wishes and warns against deciding from the schedule alone. A schedule cannot replace asking the person.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-237.reading:
Worker A: I checked the bathroom supplies with the person responsible.
Worker B: So you know the resident’s wishes too?
Worker A: No, only the quantity of supplies. I haven’t asked their wishes yet.
Worker B: I will ask the person directly.
Worker A: Yes. Please don’t decide from the schedule alone.
Worker B: Equipment checks and personal choices are separate.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-239.prompt: What division of tasks did the person and worker confirm?
options: The person will count and write the list; the worker is assigned carrying.
The person will count then carry to the shelf; the worker writes.
The person counts and the worker writes the list. Someone else is needed for carrying.
The person only carries and leaves counting to staff.
rationales: The worker writes. Someone else is requested for carrying, but no carrier is identified.
Writing responsibility is correct, but the person declines carrying and offers only counting.
The person accepts counting only and requests another carrier. The worker explicitly writes the list; carrying responsibility remains undecided.
The person can help count and declines carrying. Accepted and declined parts are reversed.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-239.reading:
Worker: We plan to make an equipment list during the household activity.
Resident: I can help count. I won’t carry things.
Worker: Will you take them to the shelf after counting?
Resident: No, only counting. Please have someone else carry them.
Worker: Understood. I will write the numbers on the list.
Resident: Then please call me when you start.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-240.prompt: How does the person want to participate in next month’s cooking activity?
options: Cook old menus while cooking staff watch the method.
Tell memories of past menus, rather than cook independently.
Ask cooking staff to implement a menu already decided.
Have cooking staff tell memories while waiting for finished food.
rationales: The person says they will tell memories rather than cook. They have no assigned cooking role.
They want to introduce old menus and memories, distinct from cooking. The menu itself is undecided.
What to cook is undecided. Discussion with cooking staff is needed, but selection and implementation requests are not complete.
The person wants to tell memories. Do not transfer that role to cooking staff.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-240.reading:
Resident: In next month’s cooking activity, I would like to introduce menus from the past.
Worker: Are you planning to cook them yourself?
Resident: Not cook; I will tell everyone my memories.
Worker: You will need time to talk with the cooking staff too.
Resident: Yes. What to make has not been decided.
Worker: I will convey your wish to introduce them and that the menu is undecided.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-241.prompt: What is the condition for using the vacuum cleaner in this scene?
options: It has reached noon, the scheduled finish time.
The schedule confirms that the next-door activity is planned until noon.
There have been no additional complaints about vacuum noise.
The responsible person confirms that the activity next door has actually ended.
rationales: Schedules may run over. The instruction requires actual completion, not time alone.
Checking a scheduled time does not establish actual completion; confirm with the responsible person.
Noise concerns are background, but the agreed condition is activity completion, not complaint numbers.
The dialogue requires checking actual completion with the responsible person rather than deciding by time. Scheduled noon and real completion are separate.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-241.reading:
Worker A: Someone said the vacuum-cleaner noise bothers them.
Worker B: Shall we use it at noon?
Worker A: Time alone does not decide it. First confirm that the activity next door has ended.
Worker B: It is scheduled until noon, but it may run over.
Worker A: Yes. Please check completion with the person responsible.
Worker B: I will distinguish scheduled time from actual completion.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-242.prompt: What does the worker mean by ‘Could you tell me?’
options: Have the person take responsibility for putting away every garment.
Have the person immediately rearrange clothes using a staff-decided method.
Ask the person to describe an arrangement that makes clothes easier to find.
Test whether the person can find clothes and ask them to report results.
rationales: The worker wants to hear the idea, not delegate the task.
This is the stage of hearing the idea. Actual placement will be discussed after organizing it; the method is not decided.
The person asks whether all tidying is requested; the worker clarifies wanting their idea. This separates sharing experience from delegation.
The request concerns explaining an idea, not testing ability and reporting it.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-242.reading:
Resident: I have a way of arranging clothes so they are easy to find.
Worker: Could you tell me about it?
Resident: Am I supposed to put everything away?
Worker: No. I want to hear your idea, not delegate the work to you.
Resident: In that case, I will describe arranging them in order of use.
Worker: After organizing what you tell me, I will discuss the actual arrangement with you.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-243.prompt: Which record accurately describes the schedule’s marks?
options: Marked areas are finished; unmarked areas have not yet been checked.
Marked areas are finished; all unmarked areas are unfinished.
Because finished areas were marked, all tidying is complete.
Because unmarked areas are unchecked, completion of marked areas is unknown too.
rationales: The person marked completed areas and has not looked at unmarked ones. This separates confirmed completion from unconfirmed details.
Unchecked unmarked areas cannot be declared unfinished. Unconfirmed and incomplete differ.
Only marked areas are established as complete. The person also asks not to report everything finished.
The person says marks show completed areas. Do not extend uncertainty elsewhere to confirmed parts.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-243.reading:
Resident: I marked the completed areas on the tidying schedule.
Worker: Thank you. Are the unmarked areas finished too?
Resident: I haven’t looked at those yet.
Worker: Now we can see which parts are finished.
Resident: Yes. Please don’t write that everything is complete.
Worker: I will record marked parts separately from unchecked parts.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-247.prompt: What does the record establish about this afternoon’s dressing?
options: Choosing a jacket independently means all afternoon dressing is independent.
Not changing jackets on some afternoons establishes that today’s change is canceled.
Morning sleeve assistance establishes consent to afternoon dressing too.
The person has not yet been asked whether they want to change this afternoon.
rationales: Choice and physical independence differ. Sleeve assistance occurs, and today’s afternoon wish remains unasked.
A usual pattern on some days is not today’s choice. Today’s wish is unconfirmed.
Morning assistance does not establish afternoon wishes or consent. The afternoon has not yet been discussed.
The record explicitly says today’s afternoon dressing preference has not been asked. It does not add wishes from morning support or usual patterns.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-247.reading:
Resident handover
For morning dressing, the person chooses the type of jacket. Staff help them put their arms through the sleeves.
On some days, they do not change jackets for afternoon activities. Today’s afternoon dressing preference has not yet been asked.
Check independent choice separately from dressing alone.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-248.prompt: Which reading of the activity record is correct?
options: Last week’s visit was shortened because explanations were difficult to hear.
Today the person is talking with a worker; afternoon-event wishes remain unchecked.
No repetition today means explanations are never repeated in large groups.
The person is visiting family in the lounge and has decided to attend the afternoon event.
rationales: The shortening reason is absent. This adds information about repetition from another setting as the cause.
Today’s conversation is with a worker, not family. Afternoon attendance remains to be asked, so neither attendance nor nonattendance is decided.
No repetition so far in today’s two-person conversation does not cancel the large-group observation. This removes conditions.
Today’s partner is a worker, not family. Afternoon participation still needs checking with the person.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-248.reading:
Activity record
Last week’s visit was shorter than planned. The reason is not given in this record.
Today the person is talking with a worker in the lounge, not visiting family.
They sometimes ask to hear explanations again in large-group activities, but so far have not done so in today’s two-person conversation.
Their wish to attend this afternoon’s event will be checked next.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-249.prompt: Which explanation of text preserves the recorded conditions?
options: Large print is readable with glasses; small print has not been tried today.
Reading large print with glasses proves small print is readable too.
Not trying small print today means no text is readable.
Reading large print proves equal reading ability without glasses.
rationales: This preserves the confirmed glasses/large-print conditions and the limit that small print was not tried today.
Small print is untried today. A large-print check cannot extend to unconfirmed small print.
Large print is recorded as readable with glasses. An unperformed check does not mean total inability.
Glasses are a recorded condition. Reading without them is not established.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-249.reading:
Reading-activity record
Text: the person can read large print while wearing glasses. Small print has not been tried today.
Audio: in a quiet room, they listen to explanations at ordinary voice volume. They report difficulty hearing corridor announcements.
Choice: ask whether they prefer larger text or a worker reading aloud.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-250.prompt: Which accurately separates roles in the gardening record?
options: Because the person wrote the name, they also wrote the date.
The person chose the pot color; the worker wrote both name and date.
The person chose the pot color and wrote the name; the worker wrote the date.
The person chose the pot color and carrier and requested the same role next time.
rationales: The person wrote the name, but staff wrote the date. Do not infer one action’s actor from another.
Staff wrote the date, but the person wrote the name. Do not transfer their action to staff.
Pot color and name were the person’s actions; date writing was staff’s. Each choice and entry matches its actual actor.
The carrier is undecided. Next-time role wishes will be asked before participation, not treated as already chosen.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-250.reading:
Gardening participation record
Pot choice: the person chose the color.
Label: the person wrote the name; a worker wrote the date.
Clearing up: who will carry equipment is undecided.
Next time: before participation, check whether the same role is wanted.

weekly-kaigo-reading-new-251.prompt: Which separates confirmed and unconfirmed details of letter contact?
options: The sister’s ability to send envelopes establishes consent to staff reading letters.
The person wants letters with their younger sister; staff reading remains unconfirmed.
Wanting letters means the person declined visits from the sister.
Envelopes arrived, so the person began writing.
rationales: The sister offered to send envelopes. That does not establish the person’s consent to staff reading.
Letter contact is a confirmed wish. Envelopes have not arrived; visit wishes and permission for staff reading remain unchecked.
Visits have not been asked about. A letter preference cannot establish refusal of visits.
Envelopes have not arrived. This changes an offer into arrival and adds writing activity.
weekly-kaigo-reading-new-251.reading:
Communication-preference interview
The person said they want to communicate by letter with their younger sister. Wishes about visits have not yet been asked.
The sister said by phone that she can send envelopes. They have not arrived yet.
Whether staff may read the letters also needs checking with the person.
